chapter: Apollo years, Eubie Blake and failing eyesight
title: Working closely with Duke Ellington
summary: Whaley tells of answering Duke's mail, copying without discussion, and Duke reversing the order of sections.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: But you sure copied a lot of -- tell us something about your relationship with Duke, since we're into this thing about your eyes, because you and him were pretty close.

Oh, yes, I used to answer all his mail and sometimes I'd get a letter, somebody would say hey, Duke, we got some girls here, come on. Shall I call them up. Yeah, call them up. And I remember in Detroit, Michigan, we had Al, what's his name, the manager. John used to --he used to hang around and the gals used to say, get rid of him and I said,
I'll see you all later, go on and leave.
But Duke was a terrific guy.
How did he talk to you about his music, that would he say to you.
He didn't say anything, just go ahead and copy it and then when he'd hear it, probably I got A, B, C, D, you know it. He'd say you start with D and go back to A and then go into E and like that.

Yeah. The way it sounded to him, so I played a number on the tape yesterday and it started with Harold a saxophone. I think Ashby was playing it, / Ashby, yeah, he was playing it and it was a long while before the whole band got in there.
Were you still copying when Ashby was in there. That's way after Bill left him.
